headline: 2,000 posts: Police start direct recruitment for ASI for first time
summary: Historically, Assistant Sub-Inspectors were only appointed via promotion from Constables. Now, the field-level role is open to direct applicants across 64 districts.
details: For the first time in the history of Bangladesh Police, the recruitment process for Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI - Unarmed) has begun through direct open examinations. Previously, direct entry was limited to Constables, Sub-Inspectors (SI), and Assistant Superintendents of Police (ASP) via BCS.

The ASI role was traditionally filled solely through the promotion of Constables. This structural change aims to integrate highly educated and skilled manpower directly into field-level administrative and investigation work to tackle evolving crime patterns.

A total of 2,000 ASI positions are being filled across 64 districts. Dhaka has the highest number of vacancies with 167, followed by Chattogram (106), Cumilla (75), Mymensingh (71), and Sylhet (48), while Bandarban has the fewest with five.

According to the Police Headquarters, 93% of the posts will be filled based on merit, while 7% are reserved for quotas. These quotas include 5% for children of freedom fighters, martyrs, and Birangonas, 1% for ethnic minorities, and 1% for persons with disabilities and the third gender.
Selected candidates will receive a salary scale of 10,200–24,680 BDT (Grade-14) and will be entitled to a monthly training allowance as per government regulations during their training period.

AIG Afrida Rubai stated that this move will accelerate administrative and operational efficiency at the field level. However, some serving Constables have expressed concern that direct recruitment might hinder their promotion opportunities and affect morale.

For the first time ever, Bangladesh Police is opening 2,000 ASI positions for direct recruitment, breaking a long-standing tradition of promotion-only entry.

The ASI role was traditionally filled solely through the promotion of Constables. This structural change aims to integrate highly educated and skilled manpower directly into field-level administrative and investigation work to tackle evolving crime patterns.

A total of 2,000 ASI positions are being filled across 64 districts. Dhaka has the highest number of vacancies with 167, followed by Chattogram (106), Cumilla (75), Mymensingh (71), and Sylhet (48), while Bandarban has the fewest with five.

According to the Police Headquarters, 93% of the posts will be filled based on merit, while 7% are reserved for quotas. These quotas include 5% for children of freedom fighters, martyrs, and Birangonas, 1% for ethnic minorities, and 1% for persons with disabilities and the third gender.

Selected candidates will receive a salary scale of 10,200–24,680 BDT (Grade-14) and will be entitled to a monthly training allowance as per government regulations during their training period.
